note: How the player's hand weapons look and sit. Issue #25: the pistol and rifle are Hyper3D models (assets/gear/,  metres, muzzle +Z) shown with its own textures (retint false). Models are CC0 (Kenney, via the MIT starter kit; see assets/third_party/kenney_starter_kit_fps/LICENSE.md) and are retinted at runtime so they read as worn gunmetal, not toys. All transforms are chest space (+Z forward, +X the character's left). Grips and muzzle are in model space, before scale.

sights.note: Iron sights in model space: front post on the sight line, rear blade pair either side of it.

cut.note: Issue #229: boxes (model space) cut from the model's mesh: its own optic block, so only our scope shows, and the front sight post, which stood in the lowered scope's view.

scope.note: Procedural scope in model space: axis along +Z at pos, rear end (eyepiece) is the ads sight. Rings on mounts down to a rail at rail_y (the receiver top, once the model's own optic is cut).

aim.note: Third person: shouldered, the butt (pivot) in the right shoulder pocket; the gun turns about it to the crosshair.

sniper_rifle.note: The fence's sniper rifle: the rifle's own model, near black (dark), a longer barrel run out of its own (barrel, model space: the model's barrel is centred at y 0.048 and ends at z 0.475, so the tube starts inside it and a collar covers the joint), and a scope whose reticle is drawn on screen as a digital one with the range to the target (digital; PlayerWeapons). ads zoom_steps: right-click aims at the first, a second right-click goes to the next, one more puts it down.

throw.note: Issue #372: the overarm grenade throw (src/systems/anim/throw_pose.gd). Hands in chest space, metres (+X the body's left, +Y up, +Z ahead; the right shoulder is at -0.22, 0.18, 0). Holding F the right hand waits at 'wind' (behind and above the shoulder, the grenade in it) and the left points ahead at 'left'. Letting go swings the right hand over 'over', through 'release' and down to 'follow' in swing_s seconds; the grenade leaves the hand release_at of the way through. The arms ease in and out over blend_s; the gun is tucked away while the hand is busy.

wheel.note: The Tab weapon wheel (issue #410). hold_time: seconds of Tab before it opens (shorter is a tap that cycles). dead_zone: fraction of the radius that is the middle. mouse_pixels: mouse travel from the middle to the rim. radius and inner are on-screen pixels.

muzzle_light.note: The flash's light. It sits `ahead` metres past the muzzle so the hand on the grip is lit warm, not blown out.

blade_volume.note: issue #16: the blade was too loud; dB for its one-shots and its hum
